summary: The v3 missing-data stack (worksheet getters -> pattern cache -> any_missing/get_priority_missing -> clean_variables) ships with several never-migrated or broken pieces that make its 'metadata-driven' claims largely dead code: (1) NA::a/NA::b is hardcoded across ~8 sites plus the worksheet QA schema while the recodeflow scoping spec (/tmp/recodeflow-pr43/missing-data.qmd) requires NA::<any lowercase>, and map_recStart_to_recEnd silently drops codes mapped to any other tag (verified: 8->NA::c vanishes without warning) -- ironically the legacy engine handles arbitrary tags; (2) missing_priority_rules.yaml does not exist in inst/ (authored in commit 370b673b with na_b=1 'Not Stated wins' but never merged), so the built-in fallback (na_a=1) silently INVERTS the documented CCHS priority -- verified: get_priority_missing(tagged_na('a'), tagged_na('b')) returns tag 'a' while the roxygen says NA::b wins -- plus a warning fires in every session and zero tests cover it; (3) Level 2A database-config-loader was never migrated, so exported get_missing_pattern_auto() always errors 'could not find function load_database_config'; (4) extract_variable_name()'s sys.call(-1) hack fails for every real call shape (cleaned$VAR gives a length-3 as.character that errors inside &&, swallowed by tryCatch) and falls back to HWTGBMI_der -- whose own pattern is EMPTY (num(0)/num(0)) because its worksheet missing rows use recStart='N/A' which should_skip_term() discards; consequently any_missing(c(6,9,2)) returns all FALSE and raw CCHS codes are never detected at Level 5 -- the pipeline works only because clean_variables() pre-tags values; (5) six process-local cache environments have no worksheet fingerprint and a fragmented clear API (verified: clear_missing_patterns_cache() leaves .complete_patterns_cache -- the one clean_variables actually reads -- populated), so mid-session worksheet edits yield mixed-version results, PSOCK workers re-derive everything and re-emit 'session' warnings per worker, and use_rdata=TRUE writes RData into the package dir at runtime (write race under parallel workers); (6) one rec_with_table(cchs2015_2016_p, ...) output empirically contains three NA representations -- haven tagged_na a/b for recoded continuous (ALWDWKY), literal 'NA(a)' factor levels for recoded categorical (ALW_1), and plain NA for derived categorical (binge_drinker: 108/200 rows lose the a/b distinction via as.factor at recode-with-table.R:953); (7) element-wise R loops make any_missing 0.28s and get_priority_missing 0.71s per 100k rows per call vs 0.007s vectorized (~40-100x), with up to ~14 calls per derived variable's case_when, plus a length-contract bug (apply_priority_hierarchy sizes output from vars[[1]] while detect_missing_vectorized uses max length).

Contrast: the LEGACY engine is generic -- /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:807-825 recode_variable_NA_formating(); verified: 'NA::c' -> tagged_na('c') for cont, 'NA(c)' for cat
Current worksheet uses only a/b (verified: recEnd NA::a 515 rows, NA::b 980 rows in inst/extdata/variable_details.csv), so no live data loss today -- the issue is structural
issues.why_design_issue: The v4/recodeflow scoping commits to NA::<any lowercase> (e.g. distinguishing Don't Know / Refusal / Not Stated, which CCHS source data actually encodes as separate codes 7/8/9). The new 'flexible' v3 infrastructure is less flexible than the 983-line legacy engine it is meant to replace, and the hardcoding is smeared across eight call sites plus the QA schema, so extending it requires coordinated edits everywhere. Worse, the failure mode is silent: a worksheet row mapped to NA::c is parsed, recognized as an NA row, and its codes discarded -- the two engines would then disagree silently about the same worksheet.
issues.candidate_fix: Replace the paired na_a_codes/na_b_codes fields with a single named structure codes_by_tag = list(a = ..., b = ..., ...) populated by one regex '^NA::([a-z])$' capture in map_recStart_to_recEnd(); priorities become a named vector from YAML/schema; get_value_priority/assign_missing/resolve_else_value iterate tags generically; widen the schema recEnd pattern to NA::[a-z]. Keep a/b as the documented CCHS convention in metadata, not code. At minimum, make unknown NA::<tag> an error rather than a silent drop.

evidence: find /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/inst -name '*.yaml' -- only documentation/metadata_registry.yaml, schemas/core/variable_details.yaml, schemas/core/variables.yaml; no schemas/cchs/ directory exists at all (ls inst/metadata/schemas/ shows only core/)
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/missing-data-functions.R:168-172 -- load_priority_rules() looks for schemas/cchs/missing_priority_rules.yaml then schemas/core/missing_priority_rules.yaml

/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/missing-data-functions.R:195-198 -- built-in fallback rules <- list(na_a = 1, na_b = 2) ('na_a higher priority as general fallback') + warning 'Priority rules YAML files not found, using built-in general fallback'

/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/missing-data-functions.R:85 -- the function's own roxygen example: 'CCHS priority: "Not Stated" (NA::b) > "Not Applicable" (NA::a)'; same documented contract in R/bmi.R:30

git show 370b673b:inst/metadata/schemas/cchs/missing_priority_rules.yaml (commit 2025-08-03, never merged to this branch) -- na_a: 2, na_b: 1, 'Not Stated highest priority ... follows StatsCan convention'. The R code was migrated; the YAML was not.

Empirical (Rscript, devtools::load_all): load_priority_rules() warns and returns $na_a 1 / $na_b 2; get_priority_missing(haven::tagged_na('a'), haven::tagged_na('b')) returns tag 'a' -- opposite of the documented CCHS hierarchy
Warning fires on first use in every session, then is suppressed by .priority_rules_cache (missing-data-functions.R:151, 200-201)
grep over tests/ -- zero references to get_priority_missing, load_priority_rules, or priority_rules: the inversion is untested and untestable-by-accident
issues.why_design_issue: A documented, methodologically deliberate semantic (item refusal is more informative than structural non-applicability, per StatsCan convention) is silently replaced by its inverse on every installation, flagged only by a session warning that reads like a config nit. Every derived variable that resolves competing missing tags via get_priority_missing() -- the smoking, ADL, alcohol, and BMI 3-step functions -- currently labels conflicted rows 'not applicable' where the design says 'not stated'. This is exactly the class of silent methodological drift the package exists to prevent.
issues.candidate_fix: Ship the YAML (recover content from git show 370b673b:inst/metadata/schemas/cchs/missing_priority_rules.yaml) into inst/metadata/schemas/cchs/ and a core/ fallback, or fold priorities into the v4 NA-pattern schema. Either way make the built-in fallback match the documented CCHS order (na_b = 1) and add a regression test asserting get_priority_missing(tagged_na('a'), tagged_na('b')) returns tag 'b'.

issues.title: Level 2A database-config-loader never migrated: exported get_missing_pattern_auto() always errors; database auto-selection degrades to lexicographic sort
evidence: grep R/: load_database_config / auto_detect_database_type are called at /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/missing-pattern-cache.R:451-465 (guarded by exists()) and :873 (UNguarded, inside get_missing_pattern_auto) but defined nowhere in R/
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/NAMESPACE:96 -- export(get_missing_pattern_auto)
Empirical (this audit): get_missing_pattern_auto('HWTGBMI_der') -> 'ERROR: could not find function "load_database_config"' -- an exported function that can never succeed
Session warning on every auto-detect path (verified): 'Database configuration functions not available. Using default CCHS configuration.' (missing-pattern-cache.R:453-456)

Fallback config (missing-pattern-cache.R:458-461) lacks type_hierarchy/naming_patterns/year_validation, so extract_years_from_database_names() returns all NA (:572-574) and select_most_recent_by_year() falls through to decreasing lexicographic sort (:650-652); observed auto-selection 'cchs2019_2020_p' for HWTGBMI_der (13 candidate databases) with warning at :477-488
File headers still declare the missing layer as a dependency: missing-pattern-cache.R:9 'DEPENDS ON: ... Level 2A (database-config-loader.R)' -- no such file in R/
issues.why_design_issue: Half of a designed configuration layer was migrated and half was not. The result is a public API that throws 'could not find function' (R CMD check cannot catch it because the call is inside a function body), exists()-guards that make behaviour depend on what happens to be in scope, and database auto-selection that silently degrades to lexicographic string ordering -- which happens to mostly work for CCHS names but is undeclared, untested behaviour that picks the alphabetically-last database, not necessarily the methodologically right one.
issues.candidate_fix: Decide in v4 scope: either migrate/reimplement the config loader (recoverable from the 3-step-tidyverse branch) or delete the dead surface -- remove get_missing_pattern_auto() and the database_config parameters, drop the exists() guards, and make the database an explicit argument (get_missing_pattern_bulk already requires it). The v4 engine should not keep exists()-based soft dependencies.

issues.title: No cache invalidation: worksheet edits mid-session yield mixed-version results; clear API is partial; .complete_patterns_cache lacks parent=emptyenv(); runtime RData writes shadow CSV edits
evidence: Cache inventory (all package-namespace environments, no worksheet fingerprint in keys): .missing_patterns_cache and .database_warnings_cache (/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/missing-pattern-cache.R:26-27), .complete_patterns_cache (:884), .priority_rules_cache (R/missing-data-functions.R:151), .cchsflow_cache$pattern_warnings (R/clean-variables.R:14-15), .variable_warnings_cache (R/worksheet-getters.R:22-23)
Keys are (variable, database) only: cache_pattern (missing-pattern-cache.R:107-134), cache_complete_pattern (:895-898, key paste(variable, database, sep='::'))

load_worksheet_metadata() re-reads the CSV on every call (R/worksheet-loaders.R:56-65; get_variable_details defaults use_rdata=FALSE at R/worksheet-getters.R:212-214) -- so after a mid-session edit to variable_details.csv, not-yet-cached variables get NEW patterns while already-cached variables keep OLD ones (get_missing_pattern short-circuits at missing-pattern-cache.R:803-806; get_complete_pattern at :940-943): one clean_variables() call can mix two worksheet versions with no warning

Partial clear API, demonstrated empirically (this audit): after get_missing_pattern('ALW_1','cchs2015_2016_p'), clear_missing_patterns_cache() leaves has_cached_complete_pattern('ALW_1','cchs2015_2016_p') TRUE -- and clean_variables() reads the COMPLETE cache (clean-variables.R:127-128 via get_complete_pattern), so the obvious exported clear function does not refresh cleaning behaviour. clear_complete_patterns_cache() (missing-pattern-cache.R:1012-1014) is separate; neither is called anywhere in R/ or tests/ (grep), and .priority_rules_cache plus the four warning caches have no public clear at all

Hygiene bug: .complete_patterns_cache <- new.env() at missing-pattern-cache.R:884 omits parent = emptyenv() (verified: parent is the package namespace, identical(parent.env(...), emptyenv()) is FALSE) and has_cached_complete_pattern (:919-922) calls exists() with default inherits=TRUE -- lookups walk the namespace chain, unlike every other cache in the stack

Warning dedup caches mean a fixed worksheet gives neither fresh patterns nor a repeat warning: clean_variables fallback warning keyed once per variable (clean-variables.R:131-138); get_variable_details not-found warning once per variable (worksheet-getters.R:257-264)

rec_with_table(variable_details = <user df>) (R/recode-with-table.R:158, 170-174) drives recode rows from the user's worksheet, but Func:: derived functions internally call clean_variables() -> get_complete_pattern() -> get_variable_details() -> load_worksheet_metadata(), which always reads the BUNDLED worksheet: a user passing a modified worksheet gets recode rules from their file and DV cleaning patterns from the package's file

save_metadata_to_rdata (R/worksheet-loaders.R:59-62, 114-125): load_worksheet_metadata(use_rdata=TRUE) WRITES <type>.RData next to the CSV at runtime -- in an installed package that is the package library (CRAN policy problem), and because RData is preferred when present (:43-53) with no mtime check, it persistently shadows later CSV edits across sessions
issues.why_design_issue: The architecture treats worksheet metadata as immutable but provides no mechanism to enforce or detect that assumption. cchsflow's own development workflow (this repo, this week) edits variable_details.csv constantly in live sessions; the result is silently inconsistent recodes that differ depending on call order. The fragmented clear API means even a user who knows about caching cannot reliably reset it, and the user-worksheet bypass breaks rec_with_table's documented contract that variable_details parameterizes the recode.
issues.candidate_fix: v4: one cache registry keyed by (worksheet fingerprint [mtime+size or hash], variable, database); load_worksheet_metadata memoizes the parsed worksheet under the same fingerprint and invalidates dependent pattern entries when it changes; single exported clear_cchsflow_caches(); thread the worksheet object (or fingerprint) explicitly through get_complete_pattern/clean_variables so user-supplied worksheets parameterize the whole pipeline; delete the runtime RData auto-save; fix parent=emptyenv() and exists(..., inherits=FALSE) on .complete_patterns_cache as an immediate v3 patch.

issues.title: Process-local caches under parallel workers: cold-start re-derivation, per-worker warning storms, serial/parallel divergence after worksheet edits, RData write races
evidence: All six caches are namespace environments created at package load (citations in previous issue) -- PSOCK/future-multisession workers each load a fresh cchsflow namespace with empty caches; nothing is shareable or precomputable because patterns exist only as side effects of first use

Cost per cold variable per worker: each get_variable_details() call re-reads the full variable_details.csv (R/worksheet-loaders.R:57, ~1.8 MB / ~3.8k rows) since use_rdata defaults FALSE (worksheet-getters.R:214) -- once per uncached variable per worker, plus pattern parsing

Once-per-session warning dedup is per-process: auto_detect_database multi-database warning (missing-pattern-cache.R:477-488), config-fallback warning (:453-456), clean_variables pattern-fallback (clean-variables.R:131-138), priority-rules fallback (missing-data-functions.R:197), variable-not-found (worksheet-getters.R:257-264) -- N workers emit N copies of each

Forked workers (mclapply) inherit the pre-fork cache snapshot copy-on-write; entries populated after fork are discarded per task. Combined with no invalidation: a parent that cached patterns before a worksheet edit keeps stale entries while fresh PSOCK workers read the edited CSV -- serial and parallel runs of the same code can return different recodes

load_worksheet_metadata(use_rdata=TRUE) auto-save (worksheet-loaders.R:59-62, 114-125): concurrent workers race writing the same <type>.RData path with non-atomic save(); failure is downgraded to a warning (:122-124)
issues.why_design_issue: Survey-scale users (multi-cycle CCHS, targets pipelines) are exactly the users who parallelize, and the v4 planning explicitly asks how caches behave under mclapply/future/targets. Today the answer is: correct only if worksheets never change, at the cost of per-worker re-derivation and duplicated warnings, with a genuine file-write race when use_rdata=TRUE.
issues.candidate_fix: Same fingerprint-keyed registry as the invalidation fix makes worker state self-consistent; precompute patterns eagerly (one bulk pass per worksheet, exported as a plain serializable object) so workers receive patterns as data rather than rebuilding them; route warnings through rlang::warn(.frequency='once') keyed on fingerprint; remove the runtime RData write.

issues.title: extract_variable_name() call-stack hack never resolves real call shapes -- every any_missing/get_priority_missing falls back to HWTGBMI_der, whose pattern is EMPTY, so raw missing codes are never detected at Level 5
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/missing-data-functions.R:218-237 -- sys.call(-1) + as.character(call_info[[2]]) + hardcoded fallback return('HWTGBMI_der'); the auto_detect=FALSE branch (:66-68, :104-106) hardcodes the same 'HWTGBMI_der' with comment 'Known variable with standard pattern'

Real call shapes: (a) cleaned$VAR -- e.g. R/smoke-intensity.R:143-144, R/smoke-start.R:237-243; verified as.character(quote(cleaned$SMKDSTY_original)) == c('$','cleaned','SMKDSTY_original'), so length-3 nchar() inside `&&` raises 'length > 1' in R>=4.2, swallowed by tryCatch -> fallback; (b) bare local parameter -- e.g. any_missing(ht, wt) at R/bmi.R:96-97 extracts 'ht', which is not a worksheet variable: verified get_missing_config('ht') warns 'Variable ht not found' then 'Could not get pattern for ht, using BMI fallback' (missing-data-functions.R:130-134) -> get_missing_pattern('HWTGBMI_der')

The fallback pattern itself is empty, verified: str(get_missing_pattern('HWTGBMI_der')) = list(na_a_codes = num(0), na_b_codes = num(0)). Cause: HWTGBMI_der has 3 worksheet rows ('[15,50]'->Func::calculate_bmi, 'N/A'->NA::a, 'N/A'->NA::b -- verified via csv module) and should_skip_term() discards recStart '^N/A$' rows (missing-pattern-cache.R:295-303), leaving no codes

Net behavioural consequence, verified: any_missing(c(6, 9, 2), c(1, 1, 1)) -> FALSE FALSE FALSE (6/9 are CCHS missing codes); get_priority_missing(c(996, 1.75), c(999, 70)) -> logical c(NA, NA). Raw CCHS missing codes are never detected by Level 5; detection works only for values already converted to tagged/plain NA by Step-1 clean_variables()
Each call also re-runs auto_detect_database over HWTGBMI_der's 13 databases with its warning machinery (missing-pattern-cache.R:408-496) -- pure overhead for an empty result
Commit 370b673b message sold this as 'Auto-detection: Variable name parsing enables metadata-driven processing' -- it is dead code in practice
issues.why_design_issue: Non-standard evaluation to guess a metadata key from the caller's source text is fragile by construction (fails for $-access, pipes, arithmetic, renamed locals) and here it fails for 100% of in-package call sites -- silently, because the error is swallowed. The entire Level 4 -> 5 'metadata integration' is inoperative; the system works only because of an undeclared contract that inputs are pre-cleaned. A function whose correctness depends on how its arguments are spelled at the call site cannot be part of a v4 public API.
issues.candidate_fix: Delete the NSE hack. Two clean options for v4: (a) make the contract explicit -- any_missing()/get_priority_missing() operate only on tagged/plain NA (documented requirement that inputs come from clean_variables()) and drop code-based detection entirely; or (b) accept an explicit pattern/variable_name argument (any_missing(..., .pattern = pat)) resolved once per derived function from the same metadata Step 1 already used. Option (a) matches actual v3 usage and is smaller.

issues.title: Two contradictory fallback patterns for unknown variables: clean_variables() invents a broad destructive CCHS pattern while Level 5 falls back to an empty one
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/clean-variables.R:127-146 -- on metadata lookup failure clean_variables() fabricates na_a={6,96,996}, na_b={7,8,9,97,98,99,997,998,999}, copy range 1-95, with a once-per-variable warning ('Using default CCHS pattern for X', suppressed afterwards via .cchsflow_cache$pattern_warnings)
/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/missing-data-functions.R:130-134 -- get_missing_config() falls back to get_missing_pattern('HWTGBMI_der'), which is empty (num(0)/num(0), verified)
So for the same unknown variable in the same pipeline: Step 1 treats 6/7/8/9/96/.../999 as missing and CONVERTS them to tagged NA; Step 2's any_missing detects no numeric codes at all

Corruption risk: clean_variables(vars = list(myvar = x)) for any variable not in variable_details.csv whose valid categories include 6-9 (CCHS has many 10+ category variables) silently converts valid responses 6,7,8,9 to tagged NA, guarded only by the once-per-session warning

The same magic numbers reappear hardcoded as terminal fallbacks in assign_missing (missing-data-functions.R:483 996L, :490 999L) and convert_tagged_na_to_original_codes (clean-variables.R:271 996, :277 999)
issues.why_design_issue: Fallbacks are where 'metadata-driven' systems leak their assumptions. Here the two halves of the 3-step pattern disagree about the same unknown variable, and the more dangerous half (destructive conversion of possibly-valid 6-9 values) is the one that fires routinely for any name typo or not-yet-migrated variable. A harmonization package whose cleaning step can silently destroy valid category codes is a correctness liability.
issues.candidate_fix: Make unknown-variable behaviour fail-closed and uniform: clean_variables() should error (or pass through untouched with one prominent warning) when no metadata exists, never invent codes; remove the empty Level-5 fallback together with the extract_variable_name hack. Where a generic CCHS pattern is genuinely wanted, require opt-in: clean_variables(..., default_pattern = cchs_single_digit()).

issues.title: Three NA representations in one rec_with_table() output: tagged_na (recoded cont), 'NA(a)'/'NA(b)' factor levels (recoded cat), plain NA (derived cat after as.factor)
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:807-825 -- recode_variable_NA_formating(): cat type -> paste0('NA(', tag, ')') string that becomes a factor LEVEL; non-cat -> haven::tagged_na(tag)

/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/recode-with-table.R:949-954 -- derived-variable dispatch: toType cat -> as.factor(unlist(...)) at :953, which collapses tagged NA doubles to plain NA (tag unrecoverable; factors store integer codes)

End-to-end, one call, verified this audit: rec_with_table(cchs2015_2016_p, c('ALW_1','ALW_2A1',...,'ALWDWKY','binge_drinker'), database_name='cchs2015_2016_p') returns ALW_1 as factor with levels [1, 2, NA(a)]; ALW_2A1..ALW_2A7 and ALWDWKY as numeric with haven tags (ALWDWKY: 41 tagged 'a', 9 tagged 'b'); binge_drinker (DerivedVar:: cat) as factor with levels [1, 2] and 108/200 PLAIN NAs -- the a/b distinction destroyed for 54% of rows

Downstream defensive shims exist precisely because of the split: coerce_cchs_label_strings (clean-variables.R:549-563) re-parses 'na(a)'/'na(b)' strings back to tagged NA; legacy-style DV functions string-match factor levels, e.g. R/education.R:59-70 (EHG2_01 == 'NA(a)' ...), R/diet.R:90-91, R/RACDPAL.R:77, R/active-transportation.R:57

User-facing gotchas: is.na() is FALSE for 'NA(b)' factor entries (ordinary levels), so naive complete-case filtering keeps them; haven::na_tag() errors on factor/logical columns ('x must be a double vector'); the three forms do not round-trip consistently through bind_rows/joins
issues.why_design_issue: Missing-data semantics is the package's core value proposition, yet what a missing value looks like depends on which of three internal code paths produced the column. Analysts must know implementation details to count missing correctly, and the derived-categorical path destroys information (the a/b distinction) that both other paths preserve. This directly blocks the v4 goal of one consistent representation per output dataframe and is the kind of inconsistency that surfaces in user bug reports and reviews.
issues.candidate_fix: Standardize on haven semantics at the engine boundary: keep categoricals as haven::labelled doubles (value labels for categories, tagged_na for missing) through the whole pipeline, converting to factor only at an explicit user-facing step (haven::as_factor, with an opt-in 'NA(x)'-level shim for v3 compatibility). Derived dispatch must stop calling as.factor on function output (recode-with-table.R:953). Plan as a documented compatibility break with a transition shim.

issues.title: Element-wise R loops in any_missing/get_priority_missing: 0.28-0.71 s per call per 100k rows (~40-100x slower than vectorized), in the hottest path of every derived variable, plus an input-length inconsistency
evidence: /Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/missing-data-functions.R:262-291 -- detect_missing_vectorized() (name notwithstanding): for (i in 1:n) over rows, inner for (var in vars), per-element haven::is_tagged_na(val), is.na(val), val %in% all_missing_codes

/Users/dmanuel/github/cchsflow/R/missing-data-functions.R:313-331 -- apply_priority_hierarchy(): same double loop calling get_value_priority() per element; :392-399 convert_to_original_format() loops again for output_format='original'

Measured (this audit, Rscript): 100,000 rows x 2 vars -- any_missing 0.282 s, get_priority_missing 0.714 s; the vectorized equivalent (x %in% codes | is.na(x), haven::is_tagged_na is vectorized) took 0.007 s -- roughly 40-100x

Call density: one case_when in a 3-step function contains several any_missing/get_priority_missing pairs (e.g. R/smoke-start.R:237-243 has 4 calls in 3 arms; adl/alcohol functions pass 5-7 variables per call); case_when evaluates every RHS fully, so a single derived variable costs seconds per 100k rows and full CCHS cycles exceed 100k rows across dozens of derived variables

Length-contract inconsistency: detect_missing_vectorized sizes output as max(sapply(vars, length)) (:253) but apply_priority_hierarchy uses n <- length(vars[[1]]) (:310-311) -- if the first argument is shorter (scalar gate), the priority result is silently truncated relative to the detection mask used in the same case_when; clean-variables.R:574-593 already has normalize_input_lengths() that neither function uses
Empirically get_priority_missing returns a LOGICAL vector (rep(NA, n) at :311) when no element is missing -- type-unstable output that only works because case_when tolerates logical NA
issues.why_design_issue: These functions sit in the innermost hot path of the 3-step architecture (every arm of every derived variable's case_when). Interpreted per-element loops over survey-scale data make the new architecture measurably slower than the legacy rowwise engine it is meant to retire, undermining the migration argument; the vars[[1]]-length and logical-NA-output quirks are latent correctness defects from the same hand-rolled iteration.
issues.candidate_fix: Rewrite both as pure vector operations: missing <- Reduce(`|`, lapply(vars, function(v) haven::is_tagged_na(v) | is.na(v) | v %in% codes)); priority via a per-variable priority matrix (vectorized tag tests) reduced with pmin/max.col; share normalize_input_lengths() so both functions recycle identically and return double vectors. Add a 1e6-row benchmark regression test.
